name: PNC-27

lead: PNC-27 fuses a piece of the p53 tumour-suppressor protein to a cell-penetrating sequence. Longevity-minded users are interested in it because lab experiments report that it ruptures cancer cells while sparing normal ones.

It is reported to bind HDM-2 protein displayed on cancer-cell membranes and form pores that cause the cell to burst. All published evidence is from cell lines and laboratory models; no human trial has been published.

paras: It is sold by research-peptide vendors and listed among longevity-oriented peptides. No appearance use is documented.
Human safety is unstudied. It is not an approved drug; it is sold as a research chemical.

angle.text: PNC-27 is a p53-derived peptide that lyses cancer cells in laboratory studies, and longevity-minded users follow it as a general-health compound. All published evidence is from cell lines; no appearance use is documented.

lead: PNC-27 is a 32-residue chimeric peptide that joins a segment of the p53 tumour-suppressor protein (residues 12-26, the region that binds HDM-2/MDM2) to a membrane-penetrating sequence [1][2]. In laboratory studies its authors report that it kills cancer cells, but not normal cells, by binding HDM-2 on the cancer-cell membrane and forming pores that lyse the cell [2][3].

All published evidence is from cell lines and laboratory models; no human clinical trial has been published. It is sold by research-peptide vendors and is not an approved medicine. The sources reviewed contain no documented looksmaxxing-community discussion; it is listed under longevity-oriented peptides.

paras: NMR studies determined the solution structure of PNC-27 and described its selective, rapid membrane-disrupting (necrotic) action on a range of human cancer cell lines [1]. A 2010 PNAS study reported that the p53 portion adopts an HDM-2-binding conformation and that the peptide kills cancer cells by binding HDM-2 in their membranes [2]. A 2022 paper describes the binding as inducing membrane-pore formation [3].

Studies of the related PNC-28 reported necrosis rather than apoptosis in pancreatic cancer cells, attributed to the penetratin sequence [4]. Work on leukemia cell lines reported dependence on membrane HDM-2 expression [5], and a separate 2020 study found membrane HDM2 on acute myeloid leukemia blasts but not on normal haematopoietic stem cells [6]. The intact peptide, rather than fragments, was reported to lyse tumour cells [7].

No studies found in humans. Laboratory research includes cell-line cytotoxicity work, a report of synergy with paclitaxel in ovarian cancer models [8], use of PNC-27 and PNC-28 as targeting moieties for gene-delivery carriers [9], and computational docking analyses [10].
PNC-27 is marketed by research-peptide suppliers for laboratory use. The sources reviewed describe no regulatory approval and no documented community protocols.

timeline.event: NMR solution structure of PNC-27 reported [1].
